output.title: When spot checks stop finding the same errors
output.body:
This is for the owner-operator of a small business, not a big governance machine. Spot checks are useful until they stop telling you anything new: the same errors keep reappearing, or new ones slip through between reviews. That is the moment the question changes from “should I inspect more?” to “which check should be automated, and which decision must stay human?”

The first good candidate is a repeatable document or data review with clear rules. Think invoice amounts against an expected limit, customer replies against a simple FAQ list, or recurring form fields that should match a known pattern. The point is not to replace judgment. It is to make routine flagging reliable so you only spend time on exceptions.

For Bareni, the useful diagnostic is a short conversation about one recurring workflow. It should answer three things: does AI fit this task at all, what is the bounded scope if it does, and what would success be measured on. That only makes sense for workflows with repeatable rules and a real handoff point. Money movement and other high-risk decisions still need human approval; that boundary stays put.

If spot checks are consuming time without catching errors consistently, the next clarity step is to name exactly which check fails most often and why.
